newsitem.title: USA: USDA says no backsliding on Canadian wheat.
newsitem.headline: USDA says no backsliding on Canadian wheat.

text.p: Deputy Agriculture Secretary Richard Rominger said Thursday the U.S. did not want any backsliding at coming wheat consultations with Canada but declined to say if a cap on shipments would be sought.
The United States has monitored shipments of Canadian wheat to U.S. markets for the past year with the warning it would act if excessive or disruptive amounts were shipped.

Rep. Earl Pomeroy, D-N.D., told Rominger during a House Agriculture Committee hearing that an explicit limit must be set. "The high tide (for Canadian sales) has been reached. We don't want any backsliding," he said.
Rominger agreed there should be no backsliding and noted the two nations, which have clashed repeatedly on the wheat issue, were due to hold consultations in the next few weeks.
Afterward, Rominger and two other USDA officials declined to say if a cap would be discussed. They said it was premature to speculate what the countries would put on the agenda.

A large number of issues probably would be discussed, Rominger said. Trade adviser Paul Drazek noted Canada was considering a number of reforms, including the operation of its Wheat Board, which could affect the nature of the talks.
